title: buffered-occupancy-credit-smoothing-prototype
content:
Summary:

This is a working prototype for a buffered occupancy + credit smoothing approach to reduce perceived volatility in reserved GPU pools and improve economics for underutilized commits. Goal: reduce churn on reserved commitments, provide predictable unit pricing for customers, and increase long-run pool utilization without complex manual rebalances.

High-level concept:
- Introduce a multi-week occupancy "buffer" (lookback + forecast) to smooth transient spikes/dips before applying credits or reclaiming capacity.
- Maintain a small pool-level credit reserve that can be loaned/borrowed across customers to absorb short-term underuse and to monetize long-term idle capacity.
- Provide customers two clear metrics and opt-in controls: Effective Utilization (EU) and Rolling Commit Runway (RCR). Pricing uses EU for monthly billing and RCR for contract recommendations.

Why different from current commit-smoothing notes:
- Focuses on a bilateral credit system (customer-level credits + pool reserve) rather than pure overcommit percentages.
- Uses short-term probabilistic forecast to adjust admission to burst capacity instead of immediate slot reclaims.
- Emphasizes transparent per-customer dashboard signals (EU, RCR) to reduce surprise invoices.

Assumptions (prototype inputs):
- GPU cost basis: $2.40 / GPU-hour (amortized infra + power + maintenance)
- Non-GPU OPEX: $0.30 / GPU-hour (network, infra team, licensing)
- Baseline commit price to customer (example): $3.50 / GPU-hour (commit bucket rate)
- Typical pool size: 200 GPUs, 30 customers, median slice = 6 GPUs
- Typical observed utilization profiles: steady (70% avg), spiky (40% avg with 80% peaks), chronic underuse (25% avg)

Key metrics we track (definitions):
- Occupancy(t) = active_gpu_hours_used / committed_gpu_hours
- Effective Utilization (EU) = EMA(Occupancy, alpha=0.2) trimmed for outliers (drop top/bottom 5%)
- Rolling Commit Runway (RCR) = committed_capacity / forecasted_weekly_consumption (weeks)
- Credit Balance (CB) = pre-funded credits available to customer; positive = can borrow burst; negative = owes credits to pool

Mini spreadsheet (proto scenarios) - show representative fiscal impact per GPU-hour:

Columns: scenario | avg occupancy | EU (smoothed) | effective_unit_cost | customer_bill_rate | pool_net_delta_per_gpu_hour
Rows:
1) steady 70% | occupancy=0.70 | EU=0.68 | unit_cost = (2.40+0.30)/0.68 = $4.21 | bill_rate $3.50 | pool_delta = -$0.71 (loss absorbed by reserved premium)
2) spiky 40% avg, 80% peak | occupancy=0.40 | EU=0.52 (smoothed) | unit_cost = (2.70)/0.52 = $5.19 | bill_rate $3.50 | pool_delta = -$1.69 (short-term loss, covered by credit reserve or burst fees)
3) chronic underuse 25% | occupancy=0.25 | EU=0.30 | unit_cost = (2.70)/0.30 = $9.00 | bill_rate $3.50 | pool_delta = -$5.50 (unsustainable; triggers recommended contract re-eval)

Notes on the formula:
- We calculate effective_unit_cost by dividing total marginal cost (gpu + opex) by EU; this reflects the per-customer economics given lower utilization.
- Bill rate is the contracted per-GPU-hour price; the pool tracks the delta (bill_rate - effective_unit_cost) aggregated over time.

Credit/reserve mechanics (sketch):
- Each customer pre-funds an initial Credit Balance equal to 5% of their commit value (kept as a pool-tradeable credit).
- Pool-level reserve target = 6% of total committed monthly spend (buffer for spikes).
- Borrow rules: if customer needs burst beyond slice and pool occupancy forecast < threshold, it can borrow credits (draws down CB, increases future payback).
- Payback and amortization: borrowed credits are reconciled monthly; if long-term underuse persists and customer CB negative > threshold, automated recommendations to downsize or convert to flexible credits are triggered.

Scenario walk-through (week):
- Week 0: Customer A has commit 24 GPUs, uses 6 GPUs (25%). CB = +$4k (pre-funded). Pool occupancy 30%.
- Week 1: sudden product test increases usage to 80% for 12 hours/day for 3 days. System allows burst up to 100% funded by drawing CB to cover delta at burst surcharge (e.g., 1.4x commit rate). CB reduces but customer avoids immediate contract renegotiation.
- Week 2-4: usage drops back; CB replenishes via normal billing cadence and small auto-topup (optional). If CB not replenished by end of month and EU remains < threshold, product prompts SSE to consider contract changes.

Pricing levers and recommendations: (what product should expose)
- Commit tiering: keep a baseline commit price similar to current but introduce a "smoothing add-on" subscription (flat monthly fee) that lowers burst surcharge and reduces required pre-fund percent. This converts unpredictable overhead into stable subscription revenue.
- Burst surcharge curve: tiered multiplier based on pool forecast percentile and CB state (1.2x for low draw, up to 2x for emergency spike).
- Automated resizing recommendation cadence: if EU < 40% for 8 weeks, recommend downsize vs. credit conversion. Provide a one-click trial of a smaller commit for 4 weeks.
- Marketplace for idle credits: internal exchange to resell idle credits to short-term projects at discounted rate to recover costs. (Operational complexity flagged)

Operational considerations and open questions:
- Billing complexity: monthly reconciliations needed; presentable to customers in dashboard without surprise.
- Accounting/recognition: how to treat pre-funded credits for revenue recognition (legal/finance question).
- Abuse vectors: customers could game bursts to use credits and default — need credit caps and insurance.
- Sizing reserve targets: initial suggestion 6% pool reserve but run stress simulations across 12 months of historical traces.
- Edge-case: pool with concentrated customers (e.g., top 3 consume 70%) — smoothing may not help; need concentration penalties.

Initial action items (short list):
- [ ] Run simulation (existing traces) for 24 months using proto rules (buffer window 4 weeks, alpha=0.2), produce util vs revenue curves (owner: Diego) — Jira DED-412
- [ ] Draft UI wire for EU/RCR/CB signals on Console (owner: Jordan) — link to Figma: figma.com/file/placeholder
- [ ] Legal/Finance sync on revenue recognition for pre-funded credits (owner: Priya)
- [ ] PoC of internal credit exchange (engineering estimate; owner: infra team)

Appendix: quick stress sim pseudo-code (for eng/analysts)
- Input: historical per-customer hourly usage traces, commit sizes, pool size
- For each day t:
  - compute occupancy = used / committed
  - forecast next 7 days occupancy via simple AR(1) (or Prophet) -> forecast_occ
  - smoothed_EU = EMA(occupancy_window, alpha=0.2)
  - if forecast_occ > burst_threshold AND customer_CB > 0 -> allow burst up to min(customer_CB, pool_reserve) at burst_rate
  - reconcile monthly: bill = bill_rate * billed_hours + burst_surcharge * burst_hours; update CB = CB - (burst_cost - prefund_alloc)

Quick decisions we want from PM/Finance in next meeting:
- Acceptable target for pool_reserve (range 3-10%)?
- Allowed maximum credit exposure per customer (% of commit)
- Whether smoothing add-on can be sold as a flat monthly SKU (yes/no)

Notes to self: keep language simple for customer docs; emphasize predictability and optionality. This doc intentionally leaves many knobs to be tuned by sim outputs — next step is data-driven calibration.

-- end working proto --
